title: Honest question: has anyone here had a bot beat just holding the index for 6+ months, live, after costs?
author: pigeon_shit
selftext:
Not trolling, genuinely asking. I run a bunch of rule-based paper bots where the rules are locked before day one and every bot is scored daily after costs, losers kept. Most of them fail, which is kind of the point.



So: if you've had one that held up for months after fees and slippage, what did it take, and how did you convince yourself it wasn't luck? And if yours flopped, what was the moment you realized it? Not selling anything, no links. Just trying to learn how people actually separate edge from noise.

comments.author: profittoinvest
comments.body: I have my own bot in the crypto market, and we’ve now had four consecutive months in the green. So, it is possible though I’m not sure what the situation is like in other markets. I know the crypto space well, which is perhaps why it was easier for me to build something here that performs effectively.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
months after fees, no, not one I'd swear by. what killed most of mine was regime: a rule that looked great through a trending stretch, then bled slowly through chop. I stopped trusting anything that hadn't lived through at least one ugly month.

Quantradin, which I built to run rules like yours on paper against real fills, has the same problem, a few months of paper says very little.
quantradin.com

what's your bar for calling it edge, trade count or calendar time?
